scenario.title: Retreat to Thessaloniki
intro.text:
RETREAT TO THESSALONIKI - 8 APR 1941

South of Doiran Lake, Central Macedonia

As expected, the Germans invaded our country in support of their unsuccessful Allies, the Italians. German armored forces, through Yugoslavia bypassing the Metaxas Line, are on their way to Thessaloniki and threaten to encircle our East Macedonia Army. I fear that we are not able to stop the Germans here. Withdraw your troops immediately to Thessaloniki and try to establish a new defense line there. Use for your non-motorized units the railway line Kilkis-Thessaloniki to escape the rapid German forces!

GOAL Retreat 22 ground units via Exit Points or hold after the eighth turn 4 VH for BV! Hold after the eighth turn 3 VH or 2 VH for V or TV!

NOTE It is advisable to delay the deployment partly until the second turn, and then to send non-motorized units immediately via train on their journey. In this mission the AI has the first turn!
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-3-0-briliant.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
line.reaction-3-0-briliant.text: All ten positions held against the Italians. Now the German columns are moving through the Balkans. Send me the transport returns; we may have to move headquarters before the next attack.
line.reaction-3-1-victory-tactical.text: We recovered the last positions and stopped the spring offensive. Headquarters is already asking which formations can move north. I haven't had time to rest them.
line.callback-0.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.callback-0.text: The Kastoria battalions heard that we took the wireless truck west. They've asked when we can reach them. The Thessaloniki officers are asking who they should call instead.
line.callback-1.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.callback-1.text: I defended going to Thessaloniki because we need the fleet. The western officers asked what transport we'd left them. I had to admit how little there was.
line.earned-decision.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.earned-decision.text: The Trebeshinë reserve is waiting beside the trucks, still under its own officers. Half the line wants its veterans; the battalion wants to remain the unit that survived together.
line.earned-decision.choice.keep-the-mou: Keep the mountain reserve as a separate battalion.
Add an experienced seven-strength mountain infantry detachment.
line.earned-decision.choice.return-the-r: Return its men and stores to the battered core.
Restore every core formation to at least eight strength and give infantry 10 experience.
line.earned-a-response.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.earned-a-response.text: Keep their number on the board. They board the trucks as a battalion and take the rear-guard assignment together.
line.earned-b-response.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.earned-b-response.text: Send the ammunition and veterans to the weakened companies before we load. Tell the reserve major where his men are going; he deserves more than a crossed-out battalion card.
line.scene-0.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.scene-0.text: Someone has painted blue arrows on the eastbound road. They are now under Greek carts, two fuel lorries, a flock of sheep, and what appears to be a municipal piano.
line.scene-1.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.scene-1.text: The piano has better road discipline than the lorries. German armoured cars are reported north of Pedino.
line.scene-2.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.scene-2.text: If we defend every junction, the fighting units queue behind their own rear guards. If we clear the road, one German patrol can turn the queue into wreckage.
line.decision.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.decision.text: Do we build a defended corridor through Pedino and Assiros, or put every serviceable truck under the combat units and shorten the rear guard?
line.decision.choice.hold-the-corridor.t: Build a defended corridor through the road junctions.
line.decision.choice.hold-the-corridor.h: Give infantry and anti-tank formations 10 experience and restore the core to at least eight strength with full ammunition.
line.decision.choice.move-the-columns.te: Give transport priority to the fighting formations and shorten the rear guard.
line.decision.choice.move-the-columns.hi: Fully refuel the core and give reconnaissance formations 15 experience.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.choice-a-0.text: A corridor, then. Give me closing hours for each junction. British traffic control can work with an hour; it cannot work with 'until the situation changes.'
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.choice-a-1.text: I'll find the men to hold them. Do not ask those men to discover their closing hour from the backs of the last trucks.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.choice-b-0.text: I'll send the rear guard on foot while the guns ride. Tell the port staff how long those men will need. They won't be arriving with the trucks.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.choice-b-1.text: I know. Combat columns move first. Broken vehicles are emptied on the spot, and nobody stops the road to save a staff car.
